dedupe_keys.name: global infrastructure risk model and resilience index giri data platform

description: GIRI is described by its producers as the first publicly available, fully probabilistic risk model estimating losses to infrastructure assets from earthquake, tsunami, landslide, riverine and coastal flood, tropical cyclone and drought for every country and territory. It covers power, telecommunications, roads and railways, water and wastewater, ports and airports, oil and gas, buildings, education and health. The model was produced for the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and is hosted on a data platform run by UNEP/GRID-Geneva; its purpose is to make contingent liabilities of national infrastructure visible and to support resilience policy. Outputs are financial risk metrics per sector and country: average annual loss (AAL), probable maximum loss (PML) and loss exceedance curves, for present climate and two climate scenarios for 2100, built on a global exposure database of geolocated assets with economic values and vulnerability functions for more than fifty infrastructure archetypes. Access is through a map viewer and risk-metric dashboards; each dataset can be downloaded as GeoTIFF with ISO 19115 metadata after filling a short form (organisation and purpose). The FAQ does not state a licence, and the platform is labelled a beta version; the composite resilience index is described but not yet published on the platform. Coarse global resolution and modelled, not observed exposure are caveats for local studies. Simulation uses are hazard exposure, multi-hazard risk and resilience screening and climate adaptation prioritisation. It is related to the CISI critical infrastructure index and to the hazard layers in this catalogue, such as Aqueduct Floods.
